correctness.rationale: The monomial-isomorphism derivation and unique diagonal normalization are algebraically explicit. Fixing a permutation reduces to equality on its offdiagonal ordered-pair orbitals, producing irreducible split-torus opens. The key orbital-rigidity argument reconstructs any prime cyclic subgroup from its directed-edge orbital partition, and composite-order fixed loci are included in prime-order ones; no nonlisted components survive. Cycle-orbit counting gives c_{p,r}=r(p-1)(2n-pr-1); any nontransposition moves at least three vertices, forcing codimension >=3n-6. Determinant has nonzero constant term on every fixed torus. Polynomial zero bounds and inclusion-exclusion prove the coefficient binom(n,2) and uniform O_n(q^{-(2n-2)}) remainder. Standalone finite verification passed, but is not used as an infinite proof. Verified limits n>=4, ordinary automorphisms, geometric reduced locus, and fixed n as q grows.

value.rationale: The full-dimensional moduli chart of full-support perfect evolution algebras has a natural exceptional-automorphism subvariety. A complete classification of its geometric irreducible components by all prime-order permutation subgroups, including exact multiplicities and codimensions for every dimension n>=4, describes the singular symmetry geography of this family. The sharp finite-field probability binom(n,2)q^{-(2n-3)}+O_n(q^{-(2n-2)}) identifies the precise leading exceptional symmetry mechanism and quantifies generic automorphism rigidity. These are natural structural/invariant consequences of the evolution-algebra monomial action, not a renaming of individual automorphism counts.
